name: Assamites of Note (Wolves at the Door Lore)

text.content:
Once a Parisian by the name of Philippe Delacroix, this @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} sorcerer of the vizier caste now goes by the Spanish rendering of his name, Don Delacruz, and holds court from a modest study in Champagne stocked with some four dozen books — his proudest possessions, by his own wry admission. His skin has darkened with age to the deep black shared by all elder Assamites regardless of birth, a fact he takes some pleasure in offering as proof against European Cainites' assumption that his clan draws only from the East. He wears a sword purely as a bluff, being "a scholar, not a killer," and keeps a cross on his wall from his mortal life as a reminder that God protects no one, living or dead, from what comes in the night.

Delacruz is known to intervene personally when the warrior caste's zeal threatens to violate the laws of hospitality — he is recorded facing down a young warrior named Karim after Karim and his students ambushed a foreign traveler for trespassing on @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite}-warded land near the Mountain. Delacruz claimed the incident as his own affair, extracted two services from the traveler in exchange for sparing his life and safe passage, and spent two nights afterward telling him of "Haqim's inheritors" — an extended apologetic for the Assamites' place among the clans, delivered with the patient, faintly mocking authority of a man who has had centuries to refine the argument. Storytellers may use Delacruz as a mouthpiece for setting the historical and cultural record straight for player characters unfamiliar with the Assamites, or as a recurring contact who owes (or is owed) a favor.
